findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/scope.md §2.5, bullet 'The Postcommunion is also a Lenten prayer in this Missal' (the words 'the Second Sunday of Lent (no. 529, p. 79, PDF p. 160)'); scope.md §3.10, 'Sources' row ('the Second Sunday of Lent (no. 529)'); research/source-bindings.toml, binding artifact.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.cmaa-facsimile-pdf, locus 'Dominica II in Quadragesima, Postcommunion Sanctificationibus tuis, printed p. 79, no. 529 (PDF p. 160), page image (reentry)'
findings.problem: The research says the 1962 Missal prints the Postcommunion 'Sanctificationibus tuis' on the Second Sunday of Lent, as no. 529. That is false. The error comes from reading the running head of printed p. 79. This reviewer read the page image of the hash-matched facsimile at PDF p. 160. No. 529 stands under the Communion 'Domine Deus meus, in te speravi' (no. 528), and after it comes the 'Super populum' prayer 'Fideles tuos' (no. 530). Only below both is the heading 'DOMINICA II IN QUADRAGESIMA', whose Introit is no. 531. So no. 529 closes the 'FORMA MISSAE BREVIOR' of the Ember Saturday of Lent, which begins on p. 77 (PDF p. 158). The running head of p. 79 names the Sunday only because the Sunday begins on that page. The Second Sunday's own Postcommunion is 'Supplices te rogamus, omnipotens Deus', no. 540 (printed p. 80, PDF p. 161). The same misreading makes the record inconsistent with itself. §2.5 calls the three 1962 loci 'the Gregorian places of §2.2', yet the Gregorianum has the prayer only at the Ember Saturday (Wilson p. 32) and at Tuesday in Holy Week (p. 47). Wilson's p. 32 even marks the following Sunday 'DIE DOMINICO UACAT'. A study drafted from this record would tell readers that the Postcommunion of the Seventeenth Sunday is also the Postcommunion of the Second Sunday of Lent. That is a false statement about the governing book.
findings.required_result: Correct scope.md §2.5 and §3.10 and the facsimile binding's locus. They must say that the typica prints 'Sanctificationibus tuis' at the Ember Saturday of Lent twice: in the full Mass (no. 516, p. 77) and in its 'forma Missae brevior' (no. 529, p. 79). It prints the prayer again, with 'sempiterna', at Tuesday of Holy Week (no. 876, p. 146). Remove every claim that the prayer belongs to the Second Sunday of Lent. Optionally record that the Second Sunday's Postcommunion is 'Supplices te rogamus' (no. 540). Keep or restate the 'Gregorian places' sentence so that it matches the corrected loci.

findings.problem: The record says the chant agrees with Theodotion's Greek against the Vulgate and the Old Greek. It cites 9:17 ἐπίφανον and 9:19 ἱλάσθητι … πρόσχες. This reviewer re-fetched Swete's two texts (hashes matched). The 9:17 contrast holds. At 9:19 the Vulgate's 'placare … attende' renders the same imperatives as Theodotion's ἱλάσθητι … πρόσχες. The Old Greek also has πρόσχες and ἱλάτευσον at 9:18-19. So 'propitius intende' does not discriminate Theodotion from the Vulgate or the Old Greek. In addition, 'illumina faciem tuam' also matches the Hebrew of 9:17 ('make thy face to shine'), which was not consulted. So the agreement at 9:17 does not by itself point to Theodotion as the source. verified.md bounds the conclusion properly, but the scope row's wording 'against the Vulgate and the Old Greek' overstates it.
findings.required_result: Restrict the 'against the Vulgate and the Old Greek' claim to 9:17 (illumina / ἐπίφανον against ostende / ἐπιβλεψάτω). Record that the 9:19 wording does not discriminate between the versions, and that the Hebrew of 9:17 was not consulted, or consult it. Keep the existing statement that the Latin version behind the compilation is unidentified.

findings.problem: The 1962 profile requires the page-2 explanatory row to give the principal modern critical horizon. It also says every date on that page must come from the chronology corpus. This reviewer ran `proper-chronology annotations` under catholic-critical-v1. It gives only 'Textual attestation: A.D. 1598' for the Epistle, Gospel and Offertory, and no critical composition date for Daniel, Ephesians or Matthew. Under the default profile, Daniel carries only the traditional 570-536 B.C. §7.4 records the missing Davidic attribution for Ps 32 and files a request for it. It does not record this parallel gap. The concise author could therefore supply a Maccabean date for Daniel from memory. §7.4 also states that the Gospel's narrated event (the Temple controversy of the Passion week) has no corpus event. Unlike the Ps 32 case, no request to the corpus owner is filed for it.
findings.required_result: Add to §7.4 that the corpus supplies no critical composition horizon for Daniel, Ephesians or Matthew under any profile. Say what page 2 may then do: name the critical position without a figure, or wait for the corpus. Either file requests with the chronology owner, for a critical Daniel horizon and for a narrated-event relation for Mt 22:34-46, citing the sources that would support them, or record why this is not done.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/scope.md §3.3 'Negative results' row and §5.2 ('Marius Victorinus, Ambrosiaster and Theodoret on Ephesians'); §3.5 'Negative results' row and §5.2 ('whether Hilary treats Pss 75 and 101 was not checked'); §3.1 and §5.2 on Hilary's Ps 118
findings.problem: §3.3 says Theodoret on Ephesians was not read because it is 'not in the library'. The library does hold it. The registered whole-volume optical layer of PG 82 (artifact.theodoret-of-cyrus.interpretatio-epistolae-ad-galatas.1864-migne-pg82-paris.ia-djvu-ocr-db2067fd) is filed under the Galatians work. This reviewer re-fetched it (SHA-256 db2067fd… matched). It carries 'ἙΡΜΗΝΕΙ͂Α ΤΗΣ ΠΡῸΣ ἘΦΕΣΙΟΥ͂Σ ΕΠΙΣΤΟΛΗΣ' at physical line 38335. The research also says it did not check whether Hilary treats Pss 75 and 101. The registered CSEL 22 record's own extent note answers that: the volume covers Pss 1, 2, 9, 13, 14, 51-69, the title of 91, and 118-150. That same registered, fetchable layer holds Hilary's Tractatus on Ps 118 (the Introit's psalm), which was left unopened. These are availability statements, not exegesis. The Epistle and the Introit already have adequate direct witnesses, so the sweep's sufficiency is unaffected.
findings.required_result: Correct the Theodoret-on-Ephesians entry. Either read PG 82 at Eph 4:1-6 and add any retained witness, or name it as registered and unread. Replace 'whether Hilary treats Pss 75 and 101 was not checked' with the extent the registered CSEL 22 record gives. Optionally read Hilary on Ps 118 (Ain, Sade) in that registered layer.

findings.problem: The second anagogical clause of reading 2 names no witness and carries no [A], [T] or [E] mark: 'the Church's confession ends in the vision of the Trinity whom the Preface adores in "distinction of persons, unity of essence, equality of majesty"'. The Preface is appointed by rubric and confesses the Trinity, but it says nothing of vision. No checked witness here carries the confession to the beatific vision, so the eschatological step is editorial. Its quoted English also matches neither the Latin nor the registered 1861 Cummiskey English ('we adore a distinction in the Persons, an unity in the essence, and an equality in the Majesty'). The first clause (the footstool, Ps 109:1, with Aquinas and Chrysostom) is grounded.
findings.required_result: Either ground the clause in a checked witness at an exact locus (for example Augustine or Aquinas on the vision of God where the record already cites them), or mark it [E]. Quote the Preface only from the Latin or from the registered Cummiskey English (praefationes-en, row 6).

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/scope.md §3.5 and interpretations.md §1.2 ('vox una, quia caro una'); scope.md §3.4 Cassiodorus ('haereditas acquisitionis … pretioso sanguine conquisivit'); scope.md §3.4 'Direct ancient exegesis, Latin' row (Irenaeus)
findings.problem: Most quotations were re-found word for word at their loci. A few in quotation marks are not exact. Augustine's En. 101 s. 1, 2 reads 'Vox ergo una, quia caro una'. Cassiodorus on Ps 32:12 reads 'haereditas est acquisitionis'. Both are quoted without the omitted word or an ellipsis. Irenaeus, Adv. haer. I.22.1, is filed under 'Direct ancient exegesis, Latin'. But he was a Greek author read in the ANF English, and there he cites Ps 32:6 as a proof-text for the rule of faith rather than expounding the psalm. Authors copy quotations from this record into the studies, so small alterations propagate.
findings.required_result: Make the quoted strings exact, or mark omissions with an ellipsis. Reclassify Irenaeus I.22.1 as Greek-patristic doctrinal use of Ps 32:6 (read in English translation), not Latin direct exegesis, and keep its use in reading 2 accordingly.

observations.note: The research-review round-0 observation said that the engine's chronology seal leaves out the Clementine book index. This reviewer traced the files the tool opens during `record --check` with a Python audit hook, and found that the book index is not the only unsealed input. The tool also opens src/sources/works/catholic-church/vulgata-clementina/editions/ebible-latvuc/artifacts/book-index-fcad78c2/book-index.tsv, 1,334 src/sources/bibles/clementine-vulgate/chapters/**.json files, and the Revised Version and World English Bible verse-text TSVs. None of them is in the sealed files or the computation inputs. The engine seals only the code, so the computation's data inputs appear unsealed. This is an engine or workflow matter, not a research-owned defect.

summary: Cold review of the research for the Claude 1962 leaf liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost (context.md, scope.md, interpretations.md, propers/verified.md and retrieved.txt, source-bindings.toml, review-dependencies.toml, chronology.toml and chronology-annotations.tex). Checks made: every sealed input re-hashed and matched; source-library validate passes; chronology record and annotations are current, and the other profiles were inspected; the whole formulary read on the facsimile's own page images at 300 dpi (hash matched); Wilson 1915 pp. 174-175, Wilson 1894 pp. 231, 232 and 359, and PL 26 cols. 165-166 and 493-496 read on page images; the patristic, medieval and liturgical quotations re-found at their loci. Those loci were Augustine En. 32, 75, 101, 109 and 118; DDC; De moribus; De pecc. mer.; Chrysostom In Mt. 71 and In Eph. 9-11; Jerome In Dan.; Gregory hom. 38 and 20; Irenaeus; Basil; Cassiodorus Pss 32, 75, 101 and 118; Aquinas Super Mt., Super Eph. and Super Ps. 32; Bellarmine; Rupert; Durandus; Gueranger; Schuster; the Sextuplex view; and Swete's Daniel. The earlier blocking findings RES-001 to RES-004 are cleared, and advisories RES-005 to RES-007 were acted on. One new blocking defect remains: the research gives the 1962 Missal's Postcommunion no. 529 to the Second Sunday of Lent. It is in fact the shorter form of the Lenten Ember Saturday. Limits of this review: the Hebrew of Daniel and the critical editions of the sacramentaries were not consulted, and the unregistered Wilson 1894 appendix p. 358, index and introduction were not re-read. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.
